_comment: layout/sar-adc-top/erc-supply-spec.json -- the `klt erc` SUPPLY SPEC this
block's T1 checklist item 11 (Power delivery, structural) is graded from.
Issue #344. JSON has no comment syntax, so every justification below lives
in a `_comment` key; `klt erc` ignores unknown keys (verified against the
pinned build in layout/erc-requirements.txt -- a run with and without these
keys produces an identical erc_findings list).
WHAT ITEM 11 GRADES (klayout-tools/docs/design-evidence-tiers.md):
- every supply declared as a nets[] entry with "kind": "supply";
- a stackup covering the layers those supplies are routed on, with
stackup[0] carrying "role": "gate";
- vias[] bridging the stackup roles;
- pass condition: every declared supply resolves to exactly ONE
electrical island -- no erc.unconnected_net and no erc.supply_short
naming it -- plus zero erc.missing_tie.
It is the STRUCTURAL question (is the supply connected to what it powers),
not the analysis question: IR-drop/EM (`klt power`) are deliberately
outside it.
LAYER PROVENANCE. Every layer/datatype pair below was resolved from TWO
independent sources and cross-checked, per issue #344's own instruction
not to copy them from another PDK's spec:
1. This repo's own pinned sky130A install (sim/pdk.json's pin, fetched
via volare): libs.tech/klayout/tech/sky130A.lyp, whose <properties>
entries name each pair directly (e.g. `met1.drawing - 68/20`,
2. klayout-tools' curated sky130 deck layer table
(klayout_tools/decks/sky130.py, EXTRACTION_DECK): active=(65,20),
The two agree on every pair used here. NOTE the label-datatype trap this
cross-check exists to catch: sky130A.lyp calls datatype 16 `*.pin` and
datatype 5 `*.label`. The TEXT this layout actually carries is on the
datatype-5 `.label` layers (confirmed by a direct text dump of the graded
GDS: 68/5, 67/5, 69/5, 71/5, 72/5, 66/5 carry text; the datatype-16 layers
carry pin POLYGONS, no text), and `klt erc`'s `label_layer` matches net
names from text -- so every `label_layer` below is the `.label` (datatype
5) layer, never the `.pin` (datatype 16) one.
SCOPE. Graded layout: whichever top-level assembly
layout/sar-adc-top/reports/LATEST names -- run-erc.sh grades that record's
sar_adc_top.gds unless handed an explicit path, and every
erc-reports/<id>/erc.json pins the exact bytes it graded in
provenance.input.content_hash. That hash, not this sentence, is what says
WHICH layout a given verdict is about; this line only names the run of
record at the time it was last written:
layout/sar-adc-top/reports/20260924-214710-b323061/sar_adc_top.gds
-- the assembly issue #362 added the drawn analog GND pad to. The stackup
covers exactly the conductor levels that layout draws -- verified with
`klt layers` on that GDS: poly/li1/met1-met5 all carry geometry, as do
licon1, mcon, via, via2, via3 and via4.

stackup.name: poly
_comment: poly.drawing 66/20 (sky130A.lyp; EXTRACTION_DECK.poly). stackup[0] and
the required "role": "gate" -- the gate-poly layer the antenna
accumulation starts from.
active_layer = diff.drawing 65/20 (sky130A.lyp; EXTRACTION_DECK.active).
Required by issue #344 for sky130 so the antenna denominator is
`poly INTERSECT diff` (real gate-oxide area) rather than raw poly area:
without it, every bare-poly shape with no gate oxide at all -- this
block draws plenty (the CDAC's SELp/SELn gate straps, std-cell tie/decap
poly) -- is counted as a gate and produces non-physical antenna ratios
(klayout-tools#1979).
label_layer = poly.label 66/5, where this layout's SELp<i>/SELn<i> gate
straps carry their text; it only populates gates[].net and moves no
finding.

stackup.name: li1
_comment: li1.drawing 67/20, li1.label 67/5 (sky130A.lyp; EXTRACTION_DECK.metals[0]
/ metal_labels[0]). sky130's local-interconnect level: the plane every
sky130_fd_sc_hd standard cell routes its own internal VPWR/VGND rail on,
so it is load-bearing for the digital half of this assembly's supply
connectivity (a text dump of the graded GDS finds 'VPWR'/'VGND' text on

stackup.name: met1
_comment: met1.drawing 68/20, met1.label 68/5 (sky130A.lyp; EXTRACTION_DECK.
metals[1] / metal_labels[1]). Carries this assembly's own 'VDD' and
'GND' text, and the std-cell macros' promoted 'VPWR'/'VGND' pin text --
i.e. every declared supply below is named on this layer.

stackup.name: met2
_comment: met2.drawing 69/20, met2.label 69/5 (sky130A.lyp; EXTRACTION_DECK.
metals[2] / metal_labels[2]). The analog sub-blocks' own pin plane
(sampling_frontend/cdac_array publish their pins here, 'VDD' included --
see layout/sar-adc-top/README.md's per-block pin geometry table).

stackup.name: met3
_comment: met3.drawing 70/20, met3.label 70/5 (sky130A.lyp; EXTRACTION_DECK.
metals[3] / metal_labels[3]). Drawn geometry: yes (1418 shapes on the
graded GDS named under SCOPE above) -- it is
both a routing plane for the analog crossings and the MiM capacitors'
bottom plate. No text is drawn on 70/5 in this layout; the label_layer is
declared anyway because a spec entry naming an absent layer is
explicitly not an error (`klt erc` shares `klt power`'s convention), and
declaring it keeps the stackup a faithful description of the process
rather than of one snapshot of this block's routing.

stackup.name: met4
_comment: met4.drawing 71/20, met4.label 71/5 (sky130A.lyp; EXTRACTION_DECK.
metals[4] / metal_labels[4]). Load-bearing for the VDD verdict, not
decorative: 'VDD' text is drawn on 71/5, and the top-level assembly
routes its analog supply across the CDAC on met4 (build_layout.py's own
met3/met4 analog-crossing convention). Dropping met4/via3 from this
stackup splits VDD into 3 islands -- measured, see the record's
record.md.

stackup.name: met5
_comment: met5.drawing 72/20, met5.label 72/5 (sky130A.lyp; EXTRACTION_DECK.
metals[5] / metal_labels[5]). The top of the sky130 stack this block
uses, and specifically where `klt place-and-route`'s PDN straps for the
two std-cell macros live -- 'VPWR'/'VGND' text is drawn on 72/5. Omitting
it would hide the digital rails from the grade entirely.

_vias_comment: Each via's layer/datatype is taken from the same two sources, and follows
sky130's own 'a via lands on the layer NUMBER of the metal below it,
datatype 44' convention (sky130A.lyp names them licon1 66/44, mcon 67/44,
.vias agree). All six are drawn in the graded layout.
licon1 is declared between poly and li1 only: diff/tap are not conductor
roles in this spec (`klt erc` is a wire/via connectivity model with no
device recognition), so a source/drain or tap licon1 simply terminates at
the li1 pad above it, which is the intended behaviour.
_nets_comment: The four supplies this block actually draws. Names are the literal label
text `klt erc` matches against the `label_layer`s above -- taken from a
direct text dump of the graded GDS, not from the schematic.
64/59) are BODY/tub labels, not routed supplies -- their layers are wells,
not conductor roles in this stackup, so declaring them would assert a
connectivity claim this model cannot make. 'VREFP'/'VREFN'/'VCM' are
reference INPUTS driven by an external source, not supplies; they are
graded as signals by item 4's LVS, not here.

nets.name: VDD
_comment: The analog 1.8 V supply: the only supply that is also a declared
top-level port of design/sar_adc_top.sch. Routed (not substrate-
synthesised) between sampling_frontend, cdac_array and comparator -- see
layout/sar-adc-top/README.md 'GND / VPWR / VGND'.

nets.name: GND
_comment: The analog ground. `.GLOBAL GND` in design/sar_adc_top.spice, so it has
no top-level port, but it is drawn: 'GND' text on met1.label 68/5.
READ THIS VERDICT NARROWLY. `klt erc` grades DRAWN conductor only. This
block's analog ground return is partly the p-substrate, which `klt
extract`'s sky130 deck synthesises as one shared `vsubs` net regardless
of drawn geometry and which no purely geometric model can see. A clean
one-island verdict on 'GND' here therefore means 'the drawn GND
conductor is one island', NOT 'every NMOS body reaches it'. The
substrate half is exactly what erc.missing_tie would have graded -- and
that check is not computed, see ties_disclosure below.

nets.name: VPWR
_comment: The std-cell digital supply rail. Declared because item 11 grades the
supply this block draws, not the supply that would pass -- hiding a
rail by not declaring it is precisely the spec-tuning issue #344
forbids -- and the declaration is UNCHANGED across the verdict it has
carried. It went in while the rail was KNOWN to fail: #344's first run
(erc-reports/20260923-143401-1ee4ba8/) reported it as two disconnected
std-cell islands reaching no top-level supply. Issue #355 then tied
both macros' met5 PDN straps into one rail and out to a top-level pin
(spec/decision-records/DR-010-digital-supply-domain-partition.md), and
it has resolved to exactly ONE island on every run since. The layout
moved; this entry did not. See the record's record.md for the verdict
of the run in hand.

nets.name: VGND
_comment: The std-cell digital ground rail; same reasoning as 'VPWR' above.

ties_disclosure.reason: No ties[] is declared, so erc.missing_tie is NOT COMPUTED for this layout -- an absence of evidence, not evidence of absence. sky130 taps ARE nameable here (tap.drawing 65/44 inside nwell.drawing 64/20, wired to li1 through licon1 66/44), so this is not an unexpressible stream; the obstacle is klayout-tools#2169, whose unisolated tie extraction collapses a real routed standard-cell design into one electrical island and reports a FALSE erc.supply_short from a correct ties[] declaration. Declaring ties[] here would therefore replace a stated gap with a misleading finding. Standing in for the ungraded check, and named so a reader can go look rather than take this on faith: (a) the two std-cell macros are tapped by klt place-and-route's own tap cells -- sky130_fd_sc_hd__tapvpwrvgnd_1 instances are present in the graded GDS by name (text.drawing 83/44 carries 'tapvpwrvgnd_1'), and 11 tap.drawing 65/44 shapes are drawn; (b) the body/tub labels VPB (nwell.label 64/5) and VNB (pwell.label 64/59) are drawn on the wells themselves; (c) the same record's LVS report (lvs.json) carries the supply nets in its net_correspondence -- VDD<->VDD (pin), and ONE digital rail, VPB|VPWR<->VPWR (pin), where issue #344's run saw a split VPWR<->VPWR_SEQ / VPWR$1<->VPWR_SELN pair, because issue #355 made the two std-cell macros' rails one net. NOTE that (c) is a partial standin only: that LVS run's own status is 'mismatch', not 'match', and neither GND nor VGND appears in its net_correspondence at all -- GND appears on the reference side of a net.merged mismatch instead, since GND and VGND extract as the single net GND|VGND.
